title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Usage Profiles and Fallback Architecture
purpose: Define the DoQ usage-profile and fallback behavior that lets strict clients fail closed while opportunistic clients record transport failures and delegate alternate DNS transport selection to callers.
design_summary: Adds DoqClientProfile enum (Strict/Opportunistic), DoqFallbackCache class for in-memory failure tracking, and profile-aware behavior to DoqClient. Strict profile fails hard on DoQ errors. Opportunistic profile records failures in the cache, backs off for a configurable period, and supports key-pinned endpoints with shortened backoff. DoqFallbackPolicy exposes the caller-owned fallback selection after a DoQ connection failure: prefer DoT when available, use cleartext DNS only when caller policy explicitly permits it, and suppress cleartext fallback for key-pinned endpoints.
data_and_state_considerations: DoqFallbackCache uses a ConcurrentDictionary for thread-safe failure tracking. The cache is shared across DoqClient instances.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Attached clients (via Attach) do not have an endpoint string; fallback checks are skipped.
Key-pinned endpoints shorten backoff to 1 minute instead of the configured period.
Cleartext fallback is never selected unless caller policy explicitly allows it, and key-pinned endpoints do not select cleartext fallback.
The backoff is advisory; callers can clear the cache to force retries.
risks: Fallback to DoT/cleartext is delegated to the caller; the adapter signals failure clearly.
The cache does not expire entries automatically; callers should manage lifecycle.

supplemental_sections.heading: Fallback Abstraction
supplemental_sections.content: No DoT or cleartext DNS client is included in this adapter. The Opportunistic profile surfaces a clear DoqException when backed off, and DoqFallbackPolicy selects the caller-owned fallback transport after a DoQ connection failure. A future slice may integrate a transport abstraction.
